scope: All 28 active registered editorial lines screened using primary 31 Oct NBS, 30 Oct Eurostat and Treasury, 28 Oct World Bank, 14 Oct IEA, 2 Oct FAO, 30 Oct WHO risk assessment, 23 Oct WHO Ebola and existing corpus. Screening does not prove absence of other events. No second thematic article meets independently verified delta/depth threshold.

reviewed_lines.note: MT-GM-2026-10-31: NBS October manufacturing 49.3, new export orders 48.7, Eurostat Q3 euro area GDP +0.4% q/q and 30 Oct Treasury 10Y 4.94%; staged EN/PT.
ICI 29 Oct US money-market assets $7.901tn (-$43.29bn week) are a fund-asset change, not cross-border flow or ownership; weekly producer owns reconciliation.
China firm-size PMI divergence (large 50.2, small 47.5) is a one-month survey; not a verified national structural transition without trade, credit and labour confirmation.
China survey and euro-area country GDP distribution screened; existing country dossiers not revised on one preliminary macro vintage.
China computing/communications manufacturing subsectors reported output and orders >=53; survey sentiment is not proof of new technical capability or deployed scale.
AI supplier contracts and capex covered in prior editions; no new independent commissioning, utilisation or productivity measurement.
Middle East energy route risks included conditionally; no independently verified new shipping throughput loss or military attribution adopted as fact.
BOJ ETF sale decision previously covered; NBS PMI cannot infer ownership/control or a new strategic actor position.
ECB 29 Oct deposit rate 2.50%, Fed 28 Oct 3.75–4.00%, US Treasury 30 Oct 10Y 4.94%; policy settings distinguished from credit conditions.
No new policy decision on 31 Oct verified; ECB/Fed/BOJ latest decisions contextualised with source dates.
No observed ex-post effect of 2027 BOJ ETF disposal or proposed China demand stimulus; not a policy-outcome study.
China survey and yield-curve data do not demonstrate a change in market design or an operational monetary experiment.
Money-fund assets, sovereign yields and equity valuations are not beneficial ownership or a completed control transfer.
No new comparable global ownership, reserve or control dataset; monthly diffusion and weekly funds cannot populate annual stocks.
NBS and Eurostat primary statistical institutions; ECB/Fed policy transmission discussed without a new institutional mandate change.
Euro-area Q3 GDP +0.4% and cross-country heterogeneity do not establish a new treaty, payment integration or trade-corridor agreement.
China high-tech PMI relative resilience does not quantify employment displacement, automation diffusion or social outcomes.

FAO September Food Price Index 136.0 (+1.5% m/m), next release 6 Nov; World Bank Oct commodity outlook food +10% 2026 forecast. Diet affordability, pesticide exposure and agricultural productivity require local price/exposure series; no new standalone causal result.

WHO/WOAH animal and human health governance, herd management, antimicrobial use, pesticide and chemical exposure screened; no newly validated veterinary outbreak or measured exposure change for separate publication.
Oil shipping risk discussed as conditional scenario with attribution and missing throughput evidence; no imminent-war claim or new deployment inferred.

WHO 30 Oct Yellow fever Africa rapid risk assessment listed; WHO 23 Oct Bundibugyo outbreak 9,704 confirmed DRC cases as of 20 Oct. Prior 26 Oct thematic staged/rejected; no new epidemic article before complete source-level verification and QA.
No newly examined primary archival evidence affecting the historical research corpus; current PMIs do not warrant intellectual-history essay.
IEA Oct Oil Market Report September stocks -10 mb and global stocks -509 mb since end-Feb; World Bank Oct energy price scenario; no new commissioned infrastructure or physical throughput proven.
Brazil 30 Oct market repricing and labour releases screened; prior post-election coverage exists, no verified new legal or fiscal action with distinct systemic delta.
World Bank commodity forecasts and IEA oil stock estimates do not establish new ownership, mineral reserve certification or sovereign resource transfer.
No new primary verified binational electricity agreement, grid commissioning or datacentre capacity; existing Itaipu/digital infrastructure research not duplicated.
China export-order PMI 48.7 and Gulf shipping exposure screened; customs export volumes and independent physical route flows not available for standalone corridor study.
IEA global oil stocks -509 mb since end-Feb (Oct14 report) and FAO price series considered; no newly comparable food/medical/mineral/energy strategic-stock inventory for cross-resource publication.
